question: Why can Arjuna not see Krishna's divine form with his own eye?
premises: Arjuna cannot see Krishna with his own eye.
Krishna gives him a divine eye to see the divine form.
inference: The verse establishes that ordinary perception must be replaced by a granted divine capacity.
uncertainties: The fused form rūpamaiśvaram is kept as one token.
plain_english: But you cannot see me with this own eye; I give you a divine eye: see my divine form.
